decision.explanation: The provided evidence from the MyPathway study (pmid-29320312) directly supports the claim that the combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab demonstrates sensitivity/response in patients with Lung Non-small Cell Carcinoma (NSCLC) harboring somatic ERBB2 (HER2) mutations. Specifically, among 14 NSCLC patients with HER2-mutated tumors, 3 patients (21%) achieved a partial response (PR) and 3 had stable disease (SD) >120 days (pmid-29320312:f02). The study design assigned patients based on HER2 mutations without amplification/overexpression (pmid-29320312:f01), confirming the molecular profile and therapy interaction. While the exact variant spelling and explicit somatic origin for the NSCLC subgroup are not detailed in the text, the study's context of HER2-mutated tumors in a clinical trial setting implies somatic origin, and the primary endpoint of sensitivity/response is clearly evidenced. The claim's core assertion of sensitivity/response to the combination therapy in this specific molecular and disease context is supported by the observed response rates.

citations.quote: The phase 2a MyPathway study assigned patients with HER2, EGFR, BRAF or SHH alterations to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab, erlotinib, vemurafenib, or vismodegib, respectively. Among thirty-six patients that received treatment with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab because of a HER2 mutation (without amplification/overexpression) four patients (11%; 95% CI, 3% to 26%) had objective responses.

Fourteen of the 36 patients with HER2-mutated tumors had NSCLC (adenocarcinoma, n = 13; adenosquamous, n = 1); in this group, three patients (21%; 95% CI, 5% to 51%) had PR and three had SD > 120 days. Only one of the other 22 patients with HER2-mutated tumors responded to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (biliary cancer).

citations.quote: The phase 2a MyPathway study assigned patients with HER2, EGFR, BRAF or SHH alterations to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab, erlotinib, vemurafenib, or vismodegib, respectively. Among thirty-six patients that received treatment with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab because of a HER2 mutation (without amplification/overexpression) four patients (11%; 95% CI, 3% to 26%) had objective responses.

Fourteen of the 36 patients with HER2-mutated tumors had NSCLC (adenocarcinoma, n = 13; adenosquamous, n = 1); in this group, three patients (21%; 95% CI, 5% to 51%) had PR and three had SD > 120 days. Only one of the other 22 patients with HER2-mutated tumors responded to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (biliary cancer).

output.explanation: The provided evidence from the MyPathway study (pmid-29320312) directly supports the claim that the combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab demonstrates sensitivity/response in patients with Lung Non-small Cell Carcinoma (NSCLC) harboring somatic ERBB2 (HER2) mutations. Specifically, among 14 NSCLC patients with HER2-mutated tumors, 3 patients (21%) achieved a partial response (PR) and 3 had stable disease (SD) >120 days (pmid-29320312:f02). The study design assigned patients based on HER2 mutations without amplification/overexpression (pmid-29320312:f01), confirming the molecular profile and therapy interaction. While the exact variant spelling and explicit somatic origin for the NSCLC subgroup are not detailed in the text, the study's context of HER2-mutated tumors in a clinical trial setting implies somatic origin, and the primary endpoint of sensitivity/response is clearly evidenced. The claim's core assertion of sensitivity/response to the combination therapy in this specific molecular and disease context is supported by the observed response rates.
